questions.stem: Why is ethanol considered a carbon neutral fuel?

options.text: It does not contain any carbon atoms
It does not produce CO2 when burned
The CO2 released when burned equals the CO2 absorbed by the plants during growth
It is made from crude oil which is carbon neutral

questions.explanation: Ethanol from fermentation is carbon neutral because the plants used to make it absorbed CO2 from the atmosphere during photosynthesis. When the ethanol is burned, the same amount of CO2 is released back. The net addition of CO2 to the atmosphere is zero.

questions.stem: What is observed when ethanol reacts with sodium metal?

options.text: The sodium floats and fizzes gently, producing hydrogen gas
The solution turns orange to green

questions.explanation: Ethanol reacts gently with sodium metal: 2C2H5OH + 2Na -> 2C2H5O-Na+ + H2. The sodium fizzes gently as hydrogen gas is produced. This reaction is much slower than sodium with water because the hydrocarbon chain in ethanol reduces reactivity.
